get.description: Liveness check. Touches no database or other dependency.

Readiness check: 200 when the database answers, 503 otherwise.

Redis is deliberately not checked: rate limiting fails open, so a Redis blip
must not take the service out of rotation.

Who the session cookie belongs to, with revocation checked.

Unlike ``GET /session`` an unverified email is allowed (``email_verified`` says
which), and the per-user limit is the API one, so a server can call it on every
request. Callers that need a verified email check the flag themselves.

post.description:
Verify a Firebase ID token (signature, expiry, revocation) and echo its identity.

Identity only, never proof of a recent sign-in: there is no freshness check and
nothing is written (sign-in and refresh keep their own checks), and an unverified
email is returned with ``email_verified`` false for the caller to act on.

put.description:
Set a new password. The current password is proven by the fresh ``id_token``.

Firebase revokes the user's refresh tokens, which includes the caller's own session:
sign in again with the new password and call ``POST /v1/auth/session`` after a 200
(the re-auth ID token predates the revoke; unverified against live Firebase).

post.description:
Everything stored about the caller: profile, settings, memberships (with the
organisation's subscription), login history and notifications. Secrets, tokens and
other users' data are never included. Rate limited; each call is audit logged.

post.description:
Create a store in PROVISIONING status (OWNER or ADMIN, within the plan limit).

Provisioning runs in the background (KAN-56). If it cannot be enqueued the store is
still created and returned with status FAILED.

patch.description: Rename (OWNER or ADMIN) or change the slug (OWNER only) of an ACTIVE store.

post.summary: Retry provisioning of a FAILED store (OWNER or ADMIN)

503.description: The change or its audit row could not be recorded and was rolled back. Retry after `Retry-After` seconds (5). If it was the step that returns a failed enqueue to FAILED, the store may stay PROVISIONING and is logged for follow-up. Also returned when the rate limiter is unavailable.

409.description: The store is not FAILED, or it was already retried the maximum number of times (3, shared with admin re-runs): `Provisioning retry limit reached`.

502.description: The job could not be enqueued. The store goes back to FAILED and the attempt does not count against the cap, unless the job already moved it on, in which case it is left as it is.
